findings.detail: CSMD1 is in H1's title, genes and mechanism ('unchecked by CSMD1 deficiency') but in no step, so its claim has no route; the cited PMID:40112933 states the link the chain needed (CSMD1 domains inhibit the classical pathway C3 convertase) and the chain never uses it.

H1.1 'C4A gene increases C4A protein' restates expression; its real claim (schizophrenia risk alleles raise C4A expression) is only in the note, so the best-supported part of H1 cannot enter the chain.
PMID:26814963 states H1.2 ('In mice, C4 mediated synapse elimination') but the run cites it only at H1.1; moved, and it is the only support H1.2 has.
PMID:22632727 shows retinogeniculate pruning depends on microglial CR3/C3 and never names C4 or C4A; PMID:40112933 is about CSMD1 inhibiting the C3 convertase and never mentions pruning.

H1.3 (excessive pruning causes schizophrenia) cites only the CSMD1 and C4A Open Targets gene scores, which say nothing about pruning; the nearest text in the run, PMID:42276261's background 'Schizophrenia pathogenesis may involve aberrant synaptic pruning', gives no direction.

Two cited texts state a direct C4-schizophrenia association (PMID:26814963: C4 alleles associate in proportion to C4A expression; PMID:42276261: C4 over-expression in schizophrenia brain), but H1 has no step that could hold it.

PMID:22632727 reports that disrupting CR3/C3 signalling leaves sustained deficits in synaptic connectivity, i.e. complement-dependent pruning is needed for normal circuits; the run cites it for excessive pruning without saying so.
H1's falsification (CSMD1 knockout in C4-overexpressing mice) tests a CSMD1-C4 interaction that no step of the chain states.
H2.1's subject is CX3CR1 alone, but its note says 'Both associated' and it cites OT:C1QA, a record about C1QA.
PMID:42276261 reports CX3CR1 under-expression in schizophrenia (blood; male brain), not that CX3CR1 loss impairs microglial function; it states H2.1 instead and was moved there.
H2.3 (C1QA activates complement) cites only the C1QA-schizophrenia Open Targets score; no cited text states it.
PMID:42276261 names excessive complement activity and altered microglial function as mediators of aberrant synaptic pruning, not of synaptic dysfunction; no H2 causal step is stated by its citations.
H2.1 ends at schizophrenia and H2.2 starts at CX3CR1 deficiency; H2.2 ends at microglial function and H2.3 starts at C1QA: H2 is two parallel arms plus a disease association, not a chain.
H2's causal steps end at synaptic dysfunction and never reach schizophrenia; the disease appears only in the unsigned association H2.1.
Every H3 step starts at NXPH3 (association, adhesion, connectivity): a star, not a chain, and the H3.2 end (adhesion and stability) is not H3.3's start.
H3's causal steps end at disrupted synaptic connectivity and never reach schizophrenia.

PMID:41333154 says only that neurexophilins, as alpha-neurexin ligands, contribute to synaptic diversity; it never names NXPH3, and the note's 'Neurexophilins stabilize alpha-neurexins at synapses' is not in the text.
H3.3 cites nothing; its own note calls it speculative.

OT:NXPH3 (score 0.0037) is cited as H3.1's chain evidence, as supporting evidence and as contradicting evidence for the same hypothesis; a near-zero score neither states the association nor reports a null, so it is excluded.
All three hypotheses are labelled support 'grounded', yet no causal step of H2 or H3 is stated by its citations, H3's only gene-disease record scores 0.00, and H1's last step has no support.
Every node except schizophrenia has an empty CURIE in the run, including the five genes.
BLN:SynapticConnectivity: no GO, HP or MP term for synaptic connectivity (circuit wiring), the end node of H3.

'impaired microglial function' and 'synaptic dysfunction' have no HP terms; I used the mouse MP terms abnormal microglial cell physiology (MP:0003691) and impaired synaptic physiology (MP:0021010) for human nodes.
The guide gives no evidence kind for an Open Targets association score; I used textMined because these rows carry only the literature (Europe PMC text-mining) datatype.

Open Targets scores of 0.00, 0.06 and 0.51 enter with the same weight when kept; the format can only support, refute or exclude a record, so the 0.0037 NXPH3 row must be excluded and a 0.06 row counts as fully as a 0.51 one.

H1's mechanism is a modifier claim (CSMD1 deficiency removes the check on C4A-driven pruning), and its falsification tests that interaction; BioLean has no form for one gene changing another's effect.
PMID:26814963's mouse result is about mouse C4, the ortholog of both human C4A and C4B; taxon 'mouse' marks the species gap but not the paralog gap.

PMID:26814963 states 'excessive complement activity in the development of schizophrenia', which as a bridge from complement activation would give C1QA a disease route; I did not add it because it bypasses H2's own end node (synaptic dysfunction) rather than filling a gap, so C1QA's disease claim stays without a route.

PMID:42276261, moved to H2.1, gives a direction (CX3CR1 under-expressed in schizophrenia), but the guide takes a direction only from a text 'cited for the step', so H2.1 stays unsigned and the CX3CR1 disease claim has no route.
The guide does not say whether 'impaired X' with no GO process for X is loss of X (invert) or an undirected change (abnormal-X phenotype); I used the abnormal phenotype, which drops 'reduced'.

The run's structured context (cell_type microglia) is on H2.2 and H2.3 but not H2.4; the guide does not say when a context field 'limits the result', and refining would disconnect H2.3 from H2.4, so I dropped it.

H2's falsification (C1QA knockdown in CX3CR1 knockout mice, read out as microglial phagocytosis of synapses) tests a CX3CR1-C1QA interaction on a node, synaptic phagocytosis, that no step of the chain contains; the chain runs the two genes in parallel to synaptic dysfunction.
sources.json gives each accession one cited_as role, so OT:NXPH3 shows only 'chain' although run.json also lists it in H3's contradicting_evidence; the contradicting role is visible only in run.json.
Splitting a compound step lists one citation once per part (PMID:42276261 under S6 and S7, PMID:41333154 under S9 and S10), so the excluded count overstates the distinct judgements.

audit.after: impairedSynapticPhysiology = MP:0021010 impaired synaptic physiology ('any functional impairment of a synapse')

The curator searched only for an 'abnormal X' term (the guide's undirected-change wording) and reported that only the 'abnormal' MP term existed. The sign stays pos and the routes are unchanged.
